The decomposer classifies Unmake's 12% under the damage.magic family — the magic-only scoping is present in the structured cache too, not only in prose. Note both atoms carry the same 700/12 pair from ONE branch, i.e. one effect surfaces twice.

sources_quoted.reads_as: Imperial Mandate has NO damage atom and no flat damage term anywhere in the current cache (the historical '5 + 6% AP bonus magic damage' Mandate is gone). Nothing in either item can produce a flat 20-damage term.

sources_quoted.text: m(R) = 100 / (100 + R) ... mitigation operator x -> x*100/(100+R) is linear in raw damage for a fixed resistance
sources_quoted.reads_as: Mitigation is linear in raw damage, so a multiplicative damage-taken amplifier composes as a clean scalar factor on the post-mitigation event value — which is why the old/new ratio can be read directly as an amp factor.

step_1_ratio.note: Exactly the Abyssal Mask Unmake factor 1.12 to display precision: 166.8 * 1.12 = 186.816 -> 186.8 (1 dp); 186.8 / 1.12 = 166.7857 -> 166.8 (1 dp).

step_2_rule_out_flat_20.observation: old - new = 20.0 exactly, so a flat-20 term is arithmetically possible.
step_2_rule_out_flat_20.rejected_because: S4 — neither Imperial Mandate nor Abyssal Mask has any flat damage term in the cache (Mandate has no damage atom at all; Unmake's only numbers are 700 units and 12 percent). A flat 20 has no source. The multiplicative 1.12 reading does.

step_3_rule_out_additive_amp_composition.test: If the engine summed amps (7% + 12% = 19%) and the fix dropped the 12%: base = 186.8 / 1.19 = 156.975; base * 1.07 = 167.96 -> 168.0, which is NOT 166.8.
step_3_rule_out_additive_amp_composition.conclusion: Amps compose multiplicatively here, and exactly one factor of 1.12 was removed.

step_4_consistent_decomposition.conclusion: Both readings agree on the same fact: the Imperial Mandate 7% Vulnerable amp (S2) is present and UNCHANGED across old and new, and precisely one Abyssal Mask 12% magic-damage factor (S1) was removed. No other quantity in either item's cached text reproduces the delta.

step_5_adjudicating_the_removed_factor.question: Is the removed 1.12 a legitimate amp on this event, or was it applied where the source forbids it?
constraints_from_sources: S1/S3: Unmake amplifies MAGIC damage only. Mandate's Vulnerable (S2) has no type qualifier. Because the Mandate factor survives unchanged while only the Abyssal factor disappears, the delta isolates exactly the one property that distinguishes the two effects in the cached text — damage-type scoping (and secondarily uniqueness/de-duplication).

S1: Unmake is unique:true and is one effect that the decomposer emits twice (control.curse AND damage.magic, S3) — a merge step that treats those as two amps double-counts 12%, and 186.8 = 148.93 * 1.12^2 is exactly that shape.

S1: Unmake does apply 'from all sources', so a change that stripped an ALLY-held curse from the attacker's MAGIC damage would contradict the source. That is the only reading under which the old value would be right.
step_5_adjudicating_the_removed_factor.resolution: Every removal mechanism supported by the cached text (magic-only scoping applied to a non-magic event; de-duplication of one effect counted twice; one unique curse instead of one per roster holder) yields the new value. The single mechanism that would vindicate the old value requires denying 'from all sources', which the cached text states explicitly and which the surviving Mandate 7% ally-amp shows is not what changed. Therefore the removed 1.12 was an over-application.

residual_uncertainty.what_i_could_not_see: The scenario definition and the event ledger live outside the permitted evidence tree (scripts/, tests/), so I could not read event[12]'s damage type, its target, or which roster member holds which item. data/ contains no golden scenario definitions (grep for 'mandate_abyssal' across the export: no hits) and data/wiki caches only an article index, no wikitext.
residual_uncertainty.falsifier: The old value 186.8 would be correct if and only if event[12] is MAGIC damage AND the Unmake curse legitimately applied exactly once to it (single in-range holder, counted once). In that case the change would be stripping an ally aura that the cached text says applies 'from all sources'.
residual_uncertainty.confidence: high on the arithmetic (the delta is exactly one Unmake 1.12 factor, and no flat/additive reading survives); moderate-to-high on the verdict, resting on the magic-only scoping in S1/S3 plus the observation that the type-agnostic Mandate amp was deliberately left in place.
